\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಸ್ವಿಚ್} (svic)}{ಸ್ವಿಚ್ (svic)}]{\kn{ಸ್ವಿಚ್} (svic) — a switch}

\label{lesson:KA-C544-svic}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for furniture, then the Kannada for to lean back.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಸ್ವಿಚ್}}
\textbf{\kn{ಸ್ವಿಚ್}} — \emph{svic} — \textquotedblleft{}a switch\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಬಾಗಿಲಿನ} \kn{ಪಕ್ಕದಲ್ಲಿ} \kn{ದೀಪದ} \kn{ಸ್ವಿಚ್} \kn{ಇದೆ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bāgilina pakkadalli dīpada svic ide.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The light switch is beside the door.
\end{quote}

\kn{ಸ್ವಿಚ್} \kn{ಹಾಕು}, to switch on; \kn{ಆನ್} \kn{ಮಾಡು} is also said.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಸ್ವಿಚ್}} (\emph{svic}) is a loan from English \emph{switch}, written with a final virama as Kannada writes many English loans.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{svic}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{svic}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bāgilina pakkadalli dīpada svic ide.} — The light switch is beside the door.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for furniture, then the Kannada for to lean back, then say \emph{svic} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಸ್ವಿಚ್} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A switch\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಪ್ಲಗ್} (plag)}{ಪ್ಲಗ್ (plag)}]{\kn{ಪ್ಲಗ್} (plag) — a plug}

\label{lesson:KA-C544-plag}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for to lean back, then the Kannada for a switch.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಪ್ಲಗ್}}
\textbf{\kn{ಪ್ಲಗ್}} — \emph{plag} — \textquotedblleft{}a plug\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಫೋನಿನ} \kn{ಚಾರ್ಜರ್} \kn{ಪ್ಲಗ್} \kn{ಸಡಿಲವಾಗಿದೆ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{phōnina cārjar plag saḍilavāgide.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The phone charger's plug is loose.
\end{quote}

\kn{ಪ್ಲಗ್} \kn{ಹಾಕು}, to plug in.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಪ್ಲಗ್}} (\emph{plag}) is a loan from English \emph{plug}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಸಿಲಿಂಡರ್} (siliṇḍar)}{ಸಿಲಿಂಡರ್ (siliṇḍar)}]{\kn{ಸಿಲಿಂಡರ್} (siliṇḍar) — a gas cylinder}

\label{lesson:KA-C544-silindar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for a switch, then the Kannada for a plug.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಸಿಲಿಂಡರ್}}
\textbf{\kn{ಸಿಲಿಂಡರ್}} — \emph{siliṇḍar} — \textquotedblleft{}a gas cylinder\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಅಡುಗೆಮನೆಯ} \kn{ಸಿಲಿಂಡರ್} \kn{ಖಾಲಿ} \kn{ಆಯಿತು}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{aḍugemaneya siliṇḍar khāli āyitu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The kitchen gas cylinder ran out.
\end{quote}

\kn{ಗ್ಯಾಸ್} \kn{ಸಿಲಿಂಡರ್}, the cooking gas cylinder.

\textbf{\kn{ಸಿಲಿಂಡರ್}} (\emph{siliṇḍar}) is a loan from English \emph{cylinder}.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಕೊಳವೆ} (koḷave)}{ಕೊಳವೆ (koḷave)}]{\kn{ಕೊಳವೆ} (koḷave) — a tube; a pipe}

\label{lesson:KA-C544-kolave}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for a plug, then the Kannada for a gas cylinder.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಕೊಳವೆ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಕೊಳವೆ}} — \emph{koḷave} — \textquotedblleft{}a tube; a pipe\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ತೋಟಕ್ಕೆ} \kn{ನೀರು} \kn{ಕೊಳವೆಯಲ್ಲಿ} \kn{ಬರುತ್ತದೆ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tōṭakke nīru koḷaveyalli baruttade.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Water comes to the garden through a pipe.
\end{quote}

\kn{ಕೊಳವೆ} \kn{ಬಾವಿ}, a borewell. \kn{ಕೊಳಲು}, the flute, comes from the same old word for a tube.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಕೊಳವೆ}} (\emph{koḷave}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 1818 lists the Kannada word for \textquotedblleft{}a tube, a blow-pipe\textquotedblright{} in the same article as the word for a flute, \kn{ಕೊಳಲು}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{koḷave}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{koḷave}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tōṭakke nīru koḷaveyalli baruttade.} — Water comes to the garden through a pipe.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for a plug, then the Kannada for a gas cylinder, then say \emph{koḷave} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಕೊಳವೆ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A tube; a pipe\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ತಂತಿ} (tanti)}{ತಂತಿ (tanti)}]{\kn{ತಂತಿ} (tanti) — a wire; a string}

\label{lesson:KA-C544-tanti}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for a gas cylinder, then the Kannada for a tube.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ತಂತಿ}}
\textbf{\kn{ತಂತಿ}} — \emph{tanti} — \textquotedblleft{}a wire; a string\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಬಟ್ಟೆ} \kn{ಒಣಗಿಸಲು} \kn{ಅಮ್ಮ} \kn{ತಂತಿ} \kn{ಕಟ್ಟಿದರು}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{baṭṭe oṇagisalu amma tanti kaṭṭidaru.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Mother tied up a wire to dry the clothes.
\end{quote}

Also a string of the veena, and in older talk a telegram.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ತಂತಿ}} (\emph{tanti}) goes back to Sanskrit \emph{tantrī}, \textquotedblleft{}the string of a lute\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 5667).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tanti}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tanti}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{baṭṭe oṇagisalu amma tanti kaṭṭidaru.} — Mother tied up a wire to dry the clothes.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for a gas cylinder, then the Kannada for a tube, then say \emph{tanti} again
\end{itemize}
